body:
Founder real-time (2026-09-12): wants an LLM-drivable procedural-texture API written in PARENA
("one shot" a texture from a prompt, save both the rendered file and the generating source --
"think GENERA OS"). Raised a real security concern mid-build ("that sounds unsafe").

Confirmed the concern was right, for a specific reason: PARENA's C emitter's #target/inline-c
escape hatch is unrestricted (checked src/emit.c directly -- inline-c is "trusted verbatim as
real C"), a genuine unsandboxed RCE vector for LLM-controlled input. Fixed per the founder's own
follow-up suggestion: compile to PARENA's Java target instead. Confirmed src/emit_java.c has zero
#target/inline-anything handling, and this target's own real construct support (scalar F64 math,
if/not, real math/* -> java.lang.Math.* lowering) makes a compiled program provably a pure
function -- no file/network/process access is even expressible in the language surface available
there. Runs in a real JVM with a capped heap + hard timeout on every subprocess.

Shipped: internal/nock/procgen.go (validate -> parena build -o X.java -> javac -> java -> PPM ->
PNG), gen_vertex.go (real Vertex AI call, same ADC pattern gfd_item_proposals.go uses), new
Layer.Source field, Service.AddProceduralLayer/RegenerateProceduralLayer/GetProceduralSource,
cmd/nock proc-add/proc-edit/proc-show, HTTP endpoints, and a real GUI panel. 13 new tests against
the real toolchain. Live-verified manually: a real checkerboard pattern from real Math.cos calls,
full pipeline PARENA->Java->JVM->PNG. go build/vet/test ./... clean.

IDUNA commit eac7a98.
